name: Bird dog
aliases: Quadruped opposite arm and leg raise

setup: On hands and knees on a mat
Hands under shoulders, knees under hips
Brace gently; back flat like a table
execution: Reach one arm forward and the other leg back
Keep your hips and shoulders level
Hold for a breath, then return slowly
faults: Don't arch your lower back as the leg rises
Don't tip your hips toward one side
Don't kick the leg up high

notes: Lift the arm and leg only as high as you can keep your back still.
A mirror, or a light stick laid along your back, helps you spot tipping or arching.
Kneel on a mat or folded towel if your knees are uncomfortable on a hard floor.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Leg-only or arm-only bird dog
regressions.reason: One limb at a time is easier to hold steady.

progressions.name: Bird dog with a longer hold
progressions.reason: Holding each rep for about 10 seconds, as in McGill's routine, adds difficulty.

substitutions.name: Dead bug
substitutions.reason: Same opposite arm and leg pattern lying on the back.

substitutions.name: Plank
substitutions.reason: Static trunk hold with no limb movement.

substitutions.name: Pallof press
substitutions.reason: Resists twisting with a loadable cable.

substitutions.name: Bear crawl
substitutions.reason: Moving version on hands and feet; harder.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at table height, figure on hands and knees on a mat, head on the right. The near arm and far leg reach so both limbs read clearly; a faint horizontal guide line along the back helps show it stays flat.

keyPositions.label: Table
keyPositions.describe: On hands and knees, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips. Back flat, head in line with the spine, eyes down.

keyPositions.label: Reach
keyPositions.describe: Near arm reaching forward level with the shoulder, far leg reaching back level with the hip, knee straight. Back still flat; hips and shoulders level; head neutral.

ikHints: Supporting hand and knee fixed in every frame
emphasise: Back stays flat while the arm and leg reach

sources.title: Harvard Health Publishing: Three moves for better spine health (McGill's Big 3)

uncertain.note: Reps may be counted per side or as total reaches; the entry doesn't fix which. Some people log it as timed holds instead.
Several joints move and the trunk holds still, so it's listed as compound; it's a low-load control exercise, not a strength lift.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data. trunkLeanFromVertical 90 means the back is horizontal.
